assessment.nobel_worthiness: Introducing firm heterogeneity and selection into trade theory changed how the field thinks about who exports, how gains from trade arise and how trade affects productivity. It also reorganised empirical work on firm-level micro data. The framework is now standard and has been tested heavily.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central contribution, and Helpman's work with Melitz and Yeaple on exporting versus FDI extends it. Credit is shared with the Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum line of work, which is not credited on this ballot. Redding is a more recent contributor, so I leave him out of the proposal.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of confirmation, with many empirical tests and refinements and a large following in policy-relevant quantification. Krugman's 2008 prize covers the earlier new trade theory, so this is a distinct advance.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would split credit between theory and empirical antecedents
How much the Helpman credit overlaps with the separate trade-policy candidate
Whether the Bernard et al. empirical antecedents deserve inclusion

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative data turned intergenerational mobility into a precisely measured, geographically resolved object. The work links it to neighbourhood causal effects and has influenced both research design and policy debate. The empirical standards are high: large samples, transparent methods and quasi-experimental validation.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the clear intellectual leader. Hendren is central to the neighbourhood-effects and causal-place work, and Friedman and Katz are important co-authors. Large team projects make individual credit harder to assign, so I restrict the proposal to two names.
assessment.maturity: Foundational papers date from about 2014 and the neighbourhood-effects work from 2018-2022. Some of this is still fairly recent, and its long-run policy relevance is not yet fully tested.
uncertainties: Whether the committee will want more time to pass
Robustness of place-effect estimates and replication by independent data users
Attribution within a large collaborative team

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kiyotaki and Moore (1997) formalised how collateral constraints propagate and amplify shocks into credit cycles. The result is a core building block of macro-finance, and it has shaped analysis of financial crises and business cycles. The mechanism is simple, general and long-lived.
assessment.attribution: The credit-cycles paper cleanly credits Kiyotaki and Moore. Gertler and Gilchrist belong to the financial accelerator line with Bernanke, who has already been recognised for related work. Excluding them keeps the proposal tight.
assessment.maturity: Nearly three decades old and widely built upon, including after the 2008 crisis. Empirical validation is indirect and comes through many derivative models.
uncertainties: Proximity to the 2022 prize on banking and financial crises
Treatment of Bernanke-Gertler-Gilchrist credit
Mostly theoretical contribution with indirect empirical tests

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Experimental evidence on reciprocity, fairness and costly punishment, together with the inequity-aversion model, shifted economic thinking about motives beyond narrow self-interest. The contribution links tractable theory to a large body of experiments and field extensions, and it is a major reference in behavioural economics.
assessment.attribution: Fehr and Schmidt (1999) is the key theoretical paper, while Fehr's broader experimental programme, with Gächter and others, is the empirical anchor. Falk is a major contributor, especially through field evidence and the preference-survey work. Bolton and Ockenfels, Rabin and others made parallel contributions that are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: More than 25 years of development with replications across many populations. Some individual findings, such as the size of effects and the stability of preferences, have been debated.
uncertainties: Parallel contributions by Rabin and Bolton-Ockenfels are not credited
Heterogeneity and context-dependence of the original lab results
Behavioural economics has already been recognised in 2002 and 2017

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The alternating-offers bargaining model gave a sharp, tractable and widely used account of how bargaining outcomes depend on patience and outside options. It underlies applied models in labour, trade, industrial organisation and finance. The extension to decentralised markets links bargaining to search.
assessment.attribution: Rubinstein (1982) is the decisive paper. Rubinstein and Wolinsky (1985) is the market extension. Binmore's contributions, including the Nash programme and implementation, are important but secondary and are not included here.
assessment.maturity: More than 40 years old and fully absorbed into the canon. The case is unusually mature, but game theory has been recognised often, most recently with the 2020 auction prize and the 2012 matching and market design prize.
uncertainties: Field concentration of past game-theory prizes
Whether Binmore or Stahl deserve joint credit
Empirical relevance is mostly through applications rather than direct tests

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Introduced a comparative empirical research programme linking legal origins and investor protection to financial development. The programme opened a large agenda in law and finance and in corporate governance. The ideas are very influential and have been heavily critiqued and refined, which is itself evidence of impact.
assessment.attribution: The core papers are La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, Shleifer and Vishny from the late 1990s. Shleifer's broader contributions are an additional consideration but sit outside this ballot. Vishny is a co-author on the core papers, so excluding him is a judgement.
assessment.maturity: Around 25-30 years since the core papers. Later critiques of the legal-origins measures and of causal interpretation weigh against it.
uncertainties: Credibility of legal-origins causal claims and the coding of the anti-director index
Treatment of Vishny
Whether recognition would rest on the full Shleifer portfolio or only this topic

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal rigidities, staggered pricing and interest-rate rules form the basis of modern monetary policy analysis in central banks. The contribution is of very high practical and scholarly importance. Many authors contributed, which makes any selection of laureates contested.
assessment.attribution: Calvo (1983) staggered pricing, Taylor's contracts and rule, and Woodford's synthesis are the clearest individual contributions. Gali, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets, among others, would make a strong alternative group. Any three-person proposal leaves out major contributors.
assessment.maturity: Decades of use, and the framework has been tested through its policy successes and failures, including the 2021-23 inflation episode. The model is now being supplemented by heterogeneous-agent versions.
uncertainties: Selection among many contributors
Performance of the framework during recent inflation
Possible displacement by heterogeneous-agent models

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Combines the task-based view of technology with credible measurement of trade-induced labour-market adjustment. It changed understanding of the distributional costs of globalisation and technology, and it has had large effects on policy and public debate. The empirical designs are transparent and heavily scrutinised.
assessment.attribution: Autor's task and polarisation work and the China-shock papers with Dorn and Hanson are the core. The task framework also draws on Acemoglu and Autor, and Acemoglu was recognised in 2024. Katz's long-running collaboration is also relevant. Naming two laureates is a conservative judgement.
assessment.maturity: The China shock paper is from 2013 and the task literature is older. Subsequent work has examined persistence, which strengthens the case, though there is continuing debate about identification and long-run effects.
uncertainties: Identification and shift-share concerns in the trade-shock designs
Overlap with prior prizes for labour and technology
Handling of Dorn and Katz in the credited group
